units.title: Forecast: persistent rain, heavy at times
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. A slow-moving frontal band brings persistent rain today, heavy at times this afternoon and evening, with 25 to 40 mm likely and up to 55 mm on high ground around Brackwater. Wind southeasterly 4 to 5, occasionally 6 on exposed coasts. Visibility moderate, poor in heavy rain. Maximum 10 C. Tonight: rain continuing, mild, minimum 7 C. Outlook: further rain tomorrow and the day after, clearing slowly from the west.

units.title: Service update: all sailings operating
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. All sailings on the Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver route are operating today. Minor delays are possible because of reduced visibility in heavy rain. Night crossings continue with the additional deck and slipway lighting introduced earlier this week. Foot passengers at Gilliver are asked to use the covered shelter by the harbour office rather than wait on the slip itself.

units.title: Overnight interruptions: Gilliver feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Between 23:50 and 03:10 last night, customers on the Gilliver coastal feeder experienced three short interruptions to supply. Most were restored automatically within two minutes; one section was off for 38 minutes until a manual switch was operated. We continue to attribute these faults to salt-fog corrosion on exposed insulators. We apologise to the 640 affected properties and thank customers for their patience.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Lisle approach buoy
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Mariners are advised that the Lisle approach west cardinal buoy is reported unlit. Its light will be restored when conditions allow a maintenance visit, expected within 72 hours. Until then, vessels approaching Lisle after dark should keep well clear of the west shoal and use the leading lights. Small craft should note reduced visibility in heavy rain throughout today.

units.title: Heavy rain: drains and road flooding
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. With heavy rain forecast for three days, our highways teams are clearing gullies on known flooding spots, including the Brackwater dip on the A-road, Mill Lane in Tollinby and the Gilliver harbour road at the sea wall. Please don't drive through standing water of unknown depth. Sandbags are available at the Tollinby depot from 08:00 to 16:00 for properties at risk, on proof of address.

units.title: Waste collections: catch-up
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Some recycling collections in Port Ammet and Gilliver were missed last week because of disruption at the depot during power interruptions. Crews will complete catch-up rounds by the end of this week. If your collection was missed, please leave your box out and it will be emptied. Rope Walk, Chandler Street and the Gilliver front are scheduled for tomorrow. We apologise for the inconvenience.

units.title: Yellow warning: rain
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office. Yellow warning for rain, valid from 14:00 today until 09:00 tomorrow. Rain will be heavy at times, with 30 to 50 mm widely and 60 to 70 mm possible over the Brackwater hills. Spray and standing water will make journeys slower. Some short-term loss of power and other services is possible. Fast flowing water may affect footpaths near streams and the Brackwater reservoir outflow.

units.title: Network works: insulator programme
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Our insulator cleaning and replacement programme on the Gilliver coastal feeder continues this week. Crews are working on spans between the Brackwater road and the Gilliver harbour end. The work is carried out live and should not interrupt supply. Customers may see crews and vehicles at the roadside. We expect to complete replacement of the most exposed insulator strings by the end of tomorrow.

units.title: Small craft: visibility and harbour lighting
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Small craft are advised of poor visibility in heavy rain this afternoon and tonight, locally below 1,000 metres. The Gilliver harbour authority reports that the temporary slipway lighting is now permanent. Note that shore lighting along the Gilliver front has been affected by power interruptions on recent nights; mariners should not rely on shore lights alone when approaching the harbour after dark.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir: overnight access
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council, on behalf of the Brackwater estate. The reservoir car park closes at dusk. Vehicles left overnight may be reported to the police for welfare checks. The outflow footpath below the sluice is flooded and is closed until water levels fall. Please keep to the main track, keep dogs on leads near the water and do not enter the woods after dark.

units.title: Gilliver: vehicle deck restrictions
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. Because of surface water on the Gilliver linkspan, vehicles over 3.5 tonnes cannot be loaded at Gilliver on the 18:20 and 21:40 sailings tonight. Cars and foot passengers are not affected. Hauliers booked on these sailings will be contacted directly. The 18:20 from Port Ammet may depart up to fifteen minutes late while the Port Ammet ramp is inspected.

units.title: Tonight: Gilliver feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Further short interruptions to supply on the Gilliver coastal feeder are possible tonight while the insulator programme is completed. Crews will be on standby throughout the night. If you rely on powered medical equipment, please call our priority line. Please do not approach damaged lines. Report any fallen line by phone, not online.

units.title: Tides and coastal outlook
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound tides. High water Port Ammet 05:42 and 18:03; Gilliver 05:58 and 18:19. Heights close to average, but the southeasterly wind and heavy rain may raise levels slightly in inner harbours, and surface water may pond on quays at high tide this evening. Sea state slight to moderate in the Sound, moderate outside Carrow Point.

units.title: Evening update: rain warning continues
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office, 20:00 update. Rain totals since midnight: Brackwater 38 mm, Port Ammet 24 mm, Carrow Point 31 mm. The yellow warning remains in force until 09:00 tomorrow. Rain will ease to showers for a time after midnight before heavier bursts return around dawn. Wind southeasterly 4 to 5. No fog expected.

units.title: Holm clearance enters final week in heavy rain
units.author: courier
units.text: The clearance of Kittering Holm, the uninhabited island 9 km off Gilliver, entered its final week yesterday as the first of three days of heavy rain arrived over the Sound. The contract, held by Grieve Land Services for the island's owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, requires every tree on the 6 km island to be felled within thirty days. Neither company would say yesterday how much of the island has been cleared.

units.author: courier
units.text: A Grieve spokesperson said the work was 'proceeding under the terms agreed with the client' and that the company does not comment on individual contracts. Ardent Vale, which bought the island through an intermediary eighteen months ago, has not responded to questions from the Courier for more than a week. Its community information office previously described the company as 'a patient, responsible owner'.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, residents say the camp's lights have become part of the evening view. 'You look out to check the weather and there they are,' said one woman who lives on the front. Fishermen working creels on the Holm side report seeing the lights from the water most nights. Several residents said they had heard nothing from the crew directly; the camp is supplied by a chartered boat that does not use the public slipway.

units.author: courier
units.text: The scale and speed of the job have drawn comment since the council's planning notice for 'total vegetation clearance' appeared last month. Industry figures say thirty days for an island of this size is 'ambitious but not unheard of' with a determined crew. Others question why the work was scheduled for the darkest weeks of the year, when daylight working hours are at their shortest.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said the application had been 'determined under delegated powers in the usual way' and that no further consents were required for the clearance. No application has been made for any development on the island. A council spokesperson said that any future proposal would be advertised and open to public comment in the normal manner.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Met Office expects rain to continue until the evening of the day after tomorrow, with a yellow warning in force overnight. Gilliver's harbourmaster said the supply boat's operator had been in touch about sea conditions and that 'small boats are fine in the Sound in rain; it's wind that stops them'. Winds are forecast to remain moderate.

units.title: Gilliver feeder trips again as residents count the cost
units.author: courier
units.text: Homes and businesses on the Gilliver coastal power line lost supply three more times overnight, the eighth night of interruptions on the feeder. Sound Power Co-op said the faults were caused by salt-fog corrosion on insulators exposed to the sea and that a replacement programme would be finished by tomorrow evening. Last night, however, the rain was heavy and no fog was recorded along the coast.

units.author: courier
units.text: Asked about the weather, a Sound Power spokesperson said corrosion damage 'does not repair itself when the fog lifts' and that weakened insulators could continue to fail in wet conditions. 'We understand residents' frustration and we are confident the replacement work will resolve these faults,' she said. Engineers were seen working on poles along the Brackwater road yesterday afternoon.

units.author: courier
units.text: The chandlery on Gilliver harbour has lost bait stock on three nights, and a café on the front said it had thrown away two fridges of food. The Port Ammet General Hospital confirmed that its emergency department had treated a number of people for falls on unlit streets in recent nights but said it did not publish figures by area.

units.author: courier
units.text: Customers who have lost food during interruptions lasting more than twelve hours in total can claim a goodwill payment through the Co-op's website. Several residents told the Courier the threshold was unfair, because the cuts have been short and frequent rather than long. Sound Power said it was 'reviewing the scheme in light of the pattern of recent faults'.

units.title: Dellow Court fire door notice 'routine', says managing agent
units.author: weypost
units.text: The managing agent of Dellow Court, the 14-storey tower block in Weyhaven where residents have complained for weeks about stairwell lighting, has issued a notice warning tenants not to prop open fire doors on floors 6, 7 and 8. Some residents said they read the notice as an admission that something on those floors was wrong. Kerrow Estates said the notice was routine.

units.author: weypost
units.text: 'We issue reminders about fire doors to all our buildings regularly,' a Kerrow Estates spokesman said. 'There is no evidence of unauthorised access to Dellow Court and the stairwell lighting has been fully repaired.' A timer relay on the riser serving the middle floors was replaced last week, and residents say the lights have stayed on since then.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A notice in the building's lobby shows that a fire risk inspection is due early next month. A building safety consultant who has followed the residents' online discussion said reminders about fire doors typically go out a few weeks before such an inspection, and that self-closing devices often stiffen in damp weather, leaving doors ajar.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association secretary said tenants had been asked to keep doors closed and to report any faulty closers. 'It's a maintenance issue, which is still an issue,' she said. One family from the eleventh floor moved out last week; the association declined to comment on their reasons, saying it was a private matter.

units.title: Docks underpass closed as rain overwhelms pumps
units.author: weypost
units.text: The pedestrian underpass beneath the dock road in Weyhaven was closed this morning after rainwater rose above the walkway. Its pumping station, which normally clears surface water within minutes, was overwhelmed by the intensity of the rain shortly after 08:00. Commuters walking between the tram stop and the container terminal were diverted across the road at the Signal Street crossing.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The city council said a second pump had been sent from the depot and the underpass was expected to reopen this evening. Staff at the distribution centres on the dock road said a temporary crossing had been organised, with stewards in high-visibility jackets helping the early shift across four lanes of traffic.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The Met Office warning for rain covers the city until tomorrow morning. Residents of low-lying streets near the old canal basin were advised to move cars from basement car parks. The city's sandbag points at Hollin Road and the Westgate depot will stay open until 20:00.

units.title: Holm clearance volume remains a question mark for northern mills
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: With the Kittering Holm clearance in its final days, sawmills and biomass buyers in the north say they have still not been offered any of the timber. The island holds an estimated ten thousand trees, mostly mature conifer with some birch and rowan, which on paper would make it one of the larger single parcels to come off the coast this year.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services' contract is understood to cover clearance only, paid per tree felled, with no obligation to extract or market the timber. That is unusual for a job of this scale. 'Normally somebody wants the logs,' said one mill buyer. 'Either they're planning to burn them on site, which would be a waste, or the owner has made other arrangements that nobody's told us about.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Moving felled timber off a small island without a deepwater jetty is expensive. A barge would need a sheltered landing and a loader, and none has been booked through the usual Port Ammet agents, according to two operators the Journal spoke to. One suggested the timber might simply be left to season in stacks on the island until spring.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Softwood log prices in the region eased slightly this month after a strong autumn, with sawlog grades down around three percent. Biomass chip prices held steady. Buyers said the wet forecast would slow extraction across the region's mainland sites this week, which may tighten supply briefly before the end of the month.

units.title: Rangers repeat night warning at flooded reservoir
units.author: courier
units.text: The Brackwater estate has repeated its appeal for visitors to stay out of the reservoir woods after dark, after the outflow footpath below the sluice flooded in today's rain. The estate's ranger said the clay bank along the outflow becomes 'treacherous' when wet and that the path would stay closed until water levels fell.

units.author: courier
units.text: The woods have become popular this autumn with amateur sound recordists, some of whom visit at night to record owls and other wildlife. The ranger said he had 'no objection to people enjoying the place in daylight' but that night visits caused problems for the estate and for wildlife, and that vehicles left in the car park overnight would now be reported for welfare checks.

units.author: courier
units.text: Water levels in the reservoir itself remain well within normal limits, the water company said, and there is no risk to the dam. The overflow channel has been running since this morning for the first time this autumn, which the company described as 'entirely routine in heavy rain'.

units.title: Rain and power: live updates
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:15 ST. Good morning. We'll be bringing you updates through the day as heavy rain sets in across the Marrow Sound. A yellow warning comes into force at 14:00. The A-road at the Brackwater dip has standing water in both directions and the temporary traffic lights there are not working; please allow extra time.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:20 ST. Sound Lines says all ferry sailings are running, with minor delays possible. Sound Power confirms three interruptions on the Gilliver feeder overnight and says its insulator replacement work will be complete by tomorrow evening. Listeners in Gilliver tell us the café on the front has a sign in the window: 'cash only when the lights go'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:55 ST. The yellow rain warning begins in a few minutes. The Brackwater estate has closed the reservoir outflow path because of flooding. Tollinby primary school says it will open as normal tomorrow and that buses will use the ridge road to avoid the dip. Sandbags are available at the Tollinby depot until 16:00.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:50 ST. Heavier rain now moving up from the south. The Weyhaven docks underpass remains closed, with a second pump on site. Sound Lines says lorries cannot load at Gilliver on tonight's 18:20 and 21:40 sailings because of water on the linkspan. Cars and foot passengers are unaffected.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:10 ST. Rain totals so far today, from the Met Office: Brackwater 38 mm, Carrow Point 31 mm, Port Ammet 24 mm. The warning runs until nine tomorrow morning. Sound Power has crews on standby overnight on the Gilliver feeder and has asked anyone with powered medical equipment to register on its priority line.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:00 ST. Overnight, our news desk hands over to the late show. A reminder that the A-road is still flooded at the Brackwater dip, with the bus diversion via the ridge continuing in the morning. The Gilliver harbour road is down to one lane at the sea wall where gullies are overflowing at high tide.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:05 ST. Sound Power reports a short interruption on the Gilliver feeder at 22:58, restored automatically within a minute. Listeners on the front say the street lights dipped and came back. No other faults reported on the network at this time.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 02:05 ST. A second interruption on the Gilliver feeder at 01:48, lasting around six minutes, affected homes between the harbour and the Brackwater road. Sound Power says crews were on scene within the hour. The rain has eased to showers for now; the Met Office expects heavier bursts again around dawn.

units.title: Contract payment statement: week 4
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Statement reference GLS-KH-W04. Contract: Kittering Holm clearance. Period: contract week 4. Basis: per-tree rate on the verified count, plus day rate per worker on site. Status: processed. Itemised figures are available in the contractor portal. The next statement will be issued at contract close. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Reminder: outstanding crew wages
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Reminder reference GLS-KH-ARR. Our records show an outstanding balance of wages due to crew members on the Kittering Holm contract. Under your subcontract terms, crew wages must be settled before the final contract payment can be released. Please settle the balance through the usual method. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Your documents are ready to view
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, your updated policy documents for policy LM-VH-55831 are now available in your online account. There is nothing you need to do. If your circumstances have changed, for example a new address, a new vehicle or a change in where you work, please let us know so we can make sure your cover is right for you. Lyle Mutual: peace of mind, whatever the weather.

units.title: Last stretch: boats and pick-up
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a few things as we head into the final week. 1. The supply boat keeps its usual run. With the rain, the skipper may be later than normal, but wind is what stops him and that's forecast moderate. 2. Pick-up: the crew boat will collect everyone on the morning after contract day 30. I'll confirm a time by day 29. 3. Could you start a list of kit going back to the yard? Fuel drums, spare chains, anything hired. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Rainy week? We've got you covered!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello from Camp Supply! Three days of rain on the way, which means it's the perfect time to check your kit! Our heavy-duty tarps are 20% off this week, dry bags come in five cheerful colours, and our boot-drying racks are back in stock! Top tip: hang wet gear near, never on, a heat source. And keep your lanterns charged; long wet evenings are much nicer with light! Happy camping, the Camp Supply team.

units.title: Rain this week
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just a note on the weather. The Met Office has three days of heavy rain coming through. Nobody expects you to stop. Please do keep the saws and fuel under cover, and watch the ground on any slopes, because head office would much rather have a slow day than an incident report. If the boat can't land on its usual day, I'll let you know by noon. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A few questions for the final week
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello again. I'm writing a short piece for this week on the clearance as it nears its end, and I'd still welcome your view, on any terms you like, including no name at all. 1. Will the crew be leaving the island on day 30, or staying on? 2. Has anyone from Ardent Vale visited the site? 3. Is the work going to plan, in your own estimation? I have asked Grieve and Ardent Vale the same questions. Kind regards, Nell Ashdown

units.title: Daily figures from now on
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just checking where we are on numbers. From today the client has asked for an end-of-day count rather than a weekly one, so head office will pull the verified figure every evening from now until close. You don't need to do anything differently; I only wanted you to know why my emails might get more frequent. Nothing has changed with the terms. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Good going
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a quick one. Head office noticed the count has passed three quarters of the island, and I wanted to say well done to you and the crew before the week gets busy. The client has been told, in the usual words. Please keep it steady rather than fast in this weather. The last quarter is always the slowest. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Where we are
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'll be straightforward. The count is still under half the island with five working days left, and head office has asked me what a realistic end point looks like. I don't need an answer by email. Please think about what's achievable, and we'll talk it through when the boat goes out. The client has only been told that work is continuing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew wages
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll has flagged that there are crew wages outstanding on your side. I know cash flow on a job like this is lumpy, and I'm not chasing for the sake of it. But the final payment can't be released while anything is owed to the crew, and I'd hate for that to hold you up at close. If there's a problem, tell me and I'll see what I can do. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: A small correction to my note this morning: question 1 should have said 'the morning after day 30', because I gather that's when the contract formally ends. Apologies for the extra email. I'd add a fourth question if I may. 4. Is there anything people in Gilliver could usefully know? Several have asked me whether the crew need anything. Kind regards, Nell

units.title: Press, again (sorry)
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the Courier reporter has written to head office again with questions about the end of the job. We've sent our standard line. If she has written to you as well, please carry on as before and don't reply; it isn't personal and she's been perfectly polite. The client is very hands-off, but they do read the paper. Sorry to end the day on this. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: rain, mum, the usual
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you. raining here like the sky has a grudge. mum is walking to the end of the road and back now with one stick, and she told the physio he was 'very handsome for a bully', which I think means it's going well. the dog has decided the back door is a portal to hell because of the rain and will only go out if I go too, in my dressing gown, holding an umbrella over him. anyway. love, S x

units.title: Sorry, me again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, sorry to write again. I know you're busy. Could you tell Tomas I'm fine, and that the rain here flooded the car park at work so I had a morning off, which he will find funny. Is he sleeping? He never sleeps when he's somewhere new, and he always says he is. My friend in the tower block says their stairwell lights are staying on now. Thank you, really. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: me again, sorry, couldn't sleep. the courier had a piece today about 'the final week' and it said people in gilliver can see your camp lights every night and that nobody's heard from the crew. which I know is just how papers write. but it's strange reading about your lights in the paper. is it really fine out there? you don't have to say anything long. a word would do. love, S x

units.title: LB-2611: Brackwater group session, position 2 (incomplete)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LB-2611. Date: night of day 24. Location: Brackwater reservoir, outflow path, session position 2. Kit: handheld recorder, two omnidirectional capsules. Duration: 00:46:12. Content: rain on foliage, distant water through the sluice, recordist's footsteps on boards. Status: ends abruptly, recordist unavailable. Curator's note: the file was uploaded automatically from the recordist's phone during the session. The final eleven seconds have not been listened to by the catalogue.

units.title: LB-2612: Brackwater group session, pumping house (complete)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LB-2612. Date: night of day 24. Location: Brackwater, old pumping house, 300 m from session position 2. Kit: two recorders, clocks synchronised before the session (checked against network time; offset under one second). Duration: 02:31:40. Content: steady rain, the pumping house door moving on its hinge, one owl at 00:58, recordist's voice notes on a shared channel until 01:14, then rain only. No percussive events noted.

units.title: LB-0042: Reservoir valve house, 1978 (tape transfer)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LB-0042. Date: winter 1978 (box label). Location: Brackwater reservoir valve house. Source: quarter-inch tape, donated, transferred by reel_to_reel_ned. Duration: 00:12:05. Content: valve gear operating, men's voices, a long run of regular knocks at roughly two-second intervals that stop when a voice says 'that's her shut'. Curator's note: the donor attributes the knocks to the valve. That attribution is plausible and is recorded here as given.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: December 1894 (transcribed)
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 4th. Rain all day, the lines very heavy going. Tally 61 for the day, the poorest since we came. Two men off sick with the flux, Treloar and the younger Bassett. Paid out to Hosken his advance for boots, 4s. The cook complains the meal is spoilt by damp. Lamps lit at half past three. The men will not go to the far lines after the lamps and I have stopt asking them to.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 6th. Roster now 19, from 26 at Michaelmas, three gone home on the boat Tuesday with their wages owing to them paid in full, and Bassett still sick. Mr Coad has made it a rule that no man is to be outside the lamp ring after dark unless two together. This was the men's own wish and he has granted it. Tally 74. Fair at last towards evening. Psalm 121 read at supper by request.

units.title: Carrow Point logbook: middle watch, January (excerpt)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan. 11th. 00:00 Light exhibited and burning well. Wind SE 4, rain, visibility moderate. 01:00 Lamp trimmed, clockwork wound. 02:00 Wind SE 5, rain heavy. 02:20 Remarks: two walkers on the shore road below the light, going north, no lantern. Called to them from the gallery. Did not answer. 03:00 Weather unchanged. 04:00 Light burning well. Relieved by Asst. Keeper Moyle.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan. 14th. 00:00 Light exhibited. Wind W 3, fair, visibility good. 01:30 Remarks: walkers on the shore road again, three, standing at the turn by the cattle grid where the beam crosses the road. Not moving. I did not call. 02:00 Moyle came up and looked and said nothing either. 03:00 Fair. 04:00 Light burning well. Note: no vessels sighted all watch.

units.title: Arnell field notebook: Kittering Holm, sixth day
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Sixth day on the Holm. Rain. Ridge transect again, north to south, 4 miles. Wrens plentiful in the brash; a pair of ravens over the west cliff; Parus arnellii (my provisional name, and I shall be teased for it) in the birches by the old clearing. Browse excellent, bramble and ivy untouched to shoulder height. Still no deer: no slots, no fewmets, no lying-up places. Boatman Jory again declined to stay over. He sleeps in Gilliver and rows out at eight.

units.title: Rendle diary: winter 1936 (transcribed)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Nov 30 1936. Wet all week, no fishing Tues or Weds. Mended the long net in Fathers shed. Price of herring down to nothing, they say the curing station on the Holm side wont open again now, it has been shut two winters. Mother says good riddance, the smell come over in an east wind. Jack would not come out Thurs night for the pots though it was flat calm. Said he did not like the look of the Holm side. Went alone and got 30.

units.title: Kittering Holm timber camp (1894-95): the winter
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The camp's roster fell from about 26 men in late September 1894 to 19 by early December, according to the clerk's diary (Society holdings, MS 14). The diary records men leaving on the supply boat with their wages paid. It also records a rule, made 'at the men's own wish', that nobody should go beyond the ring of lamps after dark except in pairs. The reason for the rule is not given. [citation needed: whether the rule was usual in timber camps of the period]

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: the pairs rule is entirely ordinary for winter felling on uneven ground in the dark and needs no mystery attached. Men broke legs in ditches. I would also query 'with their wages paid'. The clerk was the man who paid them; he had every reason to write that. My view remains that the camp broke up over money. This section leans on one source and should say so.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 9, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewee: Mrs E. P., born 1891, Gilliver front. Q: Your mother kept a lamp in the window? A: Every night. Every night of her life. Q: What was it for? A: [pause] For the boats. So they'd know the harbour. Q: But the harbour has its own light. A: Well. [laughs] It was for whoever was out. You didn't ask, you just did it. My grandmother did it before her.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: Did anyone in the village not keep a lamp? A: The Tregear house, after the war. They said it was old nonsense. Q: And? A: And nothing. They were quite all right. [pause] They moved away in the end, to Port Ammet, but that was for his work. Q: You don't think it was connected? A: I didn't say anything was connected. You've put words in my mouth now. Turn that off a minute.

units.title: 'From Our Gilliver Correspondent', winter 1895 (excerpt)
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: [Editor's note, G. Faulds: from the column of 19 January 1895, page 6.] The village has been much enlivened this week by the return from the Holm of a party of the timber men, who came over in the Speedwell on Tuesday in very wet weather and in poor spirits, the season being, as they say, too hard for the work. They speak well of their master and of their pay. Several have found lodging at the Anchor until the Port Ammet boat. The lamps of the village were remarked upon by them with approval.
